title: The Two Travelers and the Axe
text:
Two men were walking together along a road. One of them spotted an axe lying in the dust, picked it up, and called out happily, "I have found an axe!"

His companion corrected him. Since they were traveling together, he said, it would be better to say that we have found an axe. The first man shrugged and kept the axe for himself.

They had not gone far when they heard shouting behind them. The owner of the axe had discovered his loss and was running after them with some of his neighbors, looking for the thief. The man holding the axe went pale. "We are lost," he said.

His companion did not move closer. No, he answered, keep to what you said before. You found the axe, so say: I am lost. When the find was good news, you did not want to share it, so do not expect to share the trouble now.
lesson: If you claim the rewards alone, you cannot expect your partners to share the risks. People stand with you in trouble when you stood with them in success.
source: Aesop's Fables, The Two Travelers and the Axe
